title: Contextuality as an External Bookkeeping Cost under Fixed Shared-State Semantics
summary: Contextuality is a central feature distinguishing quantum from classical probability theories, but its operational meaning is often stated only qualitatively. In this Letter, we study a simple information-theoretic question: how much additional contextual information must a classical simulation introduce when it tries to keep a shared internal description fixed across contexts? To make this question precise, we analyze a minimal external-label simulation model in which the remaining context dependence is carried only by an auxiliary label.
